metadata.creator: Department of State
metadata.description: A Department of State document reproduces a request from the American Ambassador to China concerning financial assistance for Chinese students and trainees admitted to American colleges and universities. The request asks colleges, universities, scholarship administrators, and businesses accepting Chinese trainees to send specific information about financial assistance and notices of admittance directly to the appropriate United States Embassy or consular office.
metadata.title: Department of State memorandum on financial assistance for Chinese students and trainees, 20 September 1945
metadata.transcript:
[page 1]
20 September 1945

Financial assistance given to students and trainees from admission of Chinese nationals to American colleges and universities

The American Ambassador to China has made the following request concerning the above two subjects:

“It would be helpful in the handling of the visa applications of Chinese students and trainees proceeding to the United States if the Department could make known as widely as possible to colleges and universities, special bodies administering scholarships, such as the China Institute, and to American business organizations accepting Chinese as trainees that advice of the grant of scholarships, fellowships, stipends and other financial assistance, [underlined: be sent directly to the Embassy or to the Consular Office of the] United States in which the applicant resides and that advice should be as specific as possible in regard to the amount of such assistance. This is necessary in order to have some assurance of the financial information and of the adequacy of the assistance.

“It would be helpful if colleges and universities could be asked to send their notices of admittance directly to the visa issuing office and not only to make the admittance of students absolute and not conditional upon the presentation of satisfactory credentials as frequently is the case.”
